record.summary: Founding mandate of the UK AI Safety Institute, formed from the Frontier AI Taskforce as the first state-backed organisation focused on advanced AI safety for the public interest. Its mission is to 'minimise surprise to the UK and humanity from rapid and unexpected advances in AI'. Its three core functions are evaluations of advanced AI systems, foundational AI safety research and information exchange. Early evaluations cover dual-use capabilities, societal impacts, system safety and security, and loss of control. The institute is not a regulator and holds no responsibility for release decisions.
record.notes: First published on GOV.UK on 2 November 2023 and presented to Parliament as Command Paper CP 960 in November 2023; GOV.UK records the update of 17 January 2024 as the addition of an AI Safety Institute page. The institute was an evolution of the Frontier AI Taskforce, announced in April 2023, whose research team became its initial core, with Ian Hogarth continuing as Chair. It was to house the secretariat for the international 'State of the Science' report on advanced AI, whose writing group Yoshua Bengio chairs. On 14 February 2025 the institute became the AI Security Institute, with a focus on serious AI risks with security implications; it now operates as a research organisation within DSIT whose stated mission is to equip governments with a scientific understanding of the risks posed by advanced AI.

summary.quote: The Institute is the first state-backed organisation focused on advanced AI safety for the public interest. Its mission is to minimise surprise to the UK and humanity from rapid and unexpected advances in AI.
It will initially perform 3 core functions:
Develop and conduct evaluations on advanced AI systems, aiming to characterise safety-relevant capabilities
Drive foundational AI safety research, including through launching a range of exploratory research projects and convening external researchers
Facilitate information exchange, including by establishing
Early evaluations by the Institute will likely cover the following 4 areas of interest.
Dual-use capabilities: As AI systems become more capable
Societal impacts: As AI is integrated into society
System safety and security: Current safeguards are unable to prevent determined actors
Loss of control: As advanced AI systems become increasingly capable

judgment.status_reasoning: A non-binding founding document, first published on 2 November 2023. DSIT's press release of 14 February 2025 (stored for this record) renamed the institute the AI Security Institute with a narrower security focus, and aisi.gov.uk gives a different mission, so the founding mandate no longer describes the body as it is; GOV.UK also marks the paper as published under the 2022 to 2024 Sunak government. 'Superseded' stands. date_last_updated stays 2024-01-17: the paper's page says 'Updated 17 January 2024', and the overview page records that update as the addition of an AI Safety Institute page.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Mandate of a state AI safety institute; in scope with no note (AGENTS.md section 10).
